status: provisional; source and originality checks not performed
central_question: When does assurance-backed induced abandonment of independent checking create a duty to support epistemically usable withdrawal?
central_claim: A provider that materially induces recipients to abandon independent checking, thereby weakening their ability to assess later claims in that domain, has a defeasible role-specific duty to support a proportionate epistemic transition.

inference_nodes.claim: Reliability assurance can invite organized reliance on the provider's continuing competence, not merely belief in isolated true statements.
inference_nodes.status: philosophical premise; needs literature and counterexample testing

inference_nodes.claim: Replacing independent checks can foreseeably reduce recipients' ability to notice, assess, or investigate later informational failures.
inference_nodes.status: conceptual and empirical premise; needs operational definition

inference_nodes.claim: A provider that materially invites or engineers this substitution has a special causal and role-based connection to the resulting transition problem.
inference_nodes.status: normative premise; boundaries against mere reliance need defense

inference_nodes.claim: A proportionate handoff, preserved evidence, or limited training can sometimes restore a minimally usable ability to assess successors without requiring permanent service or full self-sufficiency.
inference_nodes.status: remedial premise; worked case is hypothetical, feasibility unverified

inference_nodes.claim: Assurance-backed reliance can create a loss in epistemic agency at withdrawal even when the provider has been truthful and no financial loss occurs.
Where the provider materially contributed to the loss and a proportionate transition measure is available, the provider is a fitting bearer of a limited transition responsibility.
Truthful notice and financial compensation may be insufficient; the provider may owe support that makes epistemic exit usable.

strongest_objection.claim: The proposal either restates general dependency repair or is defeated by informed, fair acceptance of specialization and shutdown risk.
assessor_sources: Astra assessment: distinguish an epistemic transition duty from general repair of induced dependence under fair allocation.
Sol assessment: test whether informed voluntary specialization and fair advance risk allocation eliminate the special duty.
strongest_objection.provisional_reply: Concede that a new irreducible duty is not established. Defend a narrower epistemic trigger and remedy: the impaired capacity is to assess later claims, and repair must restore a usable route to judgment. Fair, feasible, reversible delegation can narrow or discharge the duty; bare advance permission may not settle whether the provider induced and controls the loss.

worked_case.case: Two equally accurate weather services; only one encourages a community to dismantle local observation capacity before shutting down.
worked_case.isolated_variable: Provider-induced loss of independent epistemic checking capacity, holding forecast accuracy and notice equal.
worked_case.predicted_difference: The service that helped remove the community's evaluative fallback may owe a proportionate handoff; the other need not rebuild capacity that remained intact.

defeaters: Informed, feasible, reversible specialization eliminates the complaint even where the provider induced the loss.
The proposed epistemic trigger and remedy add no guidance beyond general dependency repair.
Recipients cannot be said to have lost a coherent evaluative capacity, or transition measures cannot restore one.
Equivalent duties arise when evaluative capacity was not impaired, showing the epistemic feature is explanatorily idle.
Closest existing literature already supplies the same trigger, scope limits, and remedy.
non_claims: No source has been read or checked in this expansion.
No originality or contest-eligibility conclusion is established.
No claim that every expert, platform, or infrastructure owes continued service.
No empirical result about actual weather-service users or providers.
